record.original_question: For products of projective spaces (and, more generally, other interesting classes of varieties), classify special line bundles in the sense that there exists r ≥ 1 for which r generic double points fail to impose independent conditions on the line bundle.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Classify special line bundles on the product of projective spaces. More generally, classify special line bundles on interesting classes of varieties.
We say that a line bundle L is special if there is r ≥ 1 such that r double points with generic supports in X do not impose independent conditions on L.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$ and let $L$ be a line bundle on $X$. For a point $p \in X$, a "double point" at $p$ is the zero-dimensional subscheme defined by the square $\mathfrak{m}_p^2$ of the maximal ideal of $p$. Given $r \ge 1$ and generic points $p_1, \dots, p_r \in X$, let $Z_r \subset X$ be the disjoint union of the corresponding double points. One says that $r$ generic double points impose independent conditions on $L$ if the natural restriction map
$$H^0(X, L) \longrightarrow H^0(X, L \otimes \mathcal{O}_{Z_r})$$
is of maximal rank, i.e. surjective or injective (equivalently, $\dim H^0(X, L \otimes \mathcal{I}_{Z_r}) = \max\{0,\; h^0(X,L) - r(\dim X + 1)\}$). The line bundle $L$ is called special if there exists some $r \ge 1$ for which $r$ generic double points fail to impose independent conditions on $L$.

Problem: Classify all special line bundles on a product of projective spaces $\mathbb{P}^{n_1} \times \cdots \times \mathbb{P}^{n_k}$. More generally, give such a classification for other natural classes of smooth projective varieties.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of classifying special line bundles (in the sense of generic double points failing to impose independent conditions, related to the classical polynomial interpolation / Alexander–Hirschowitz-type problems) is a long-standing open problem. While the Alexander–Hirschowitz theorem solves the case of $\mathbb{P}^n$ with the standard line bundles, the analogous classification for products of projective spaces and other varieties remains open in general; only partial results (e.g., for specific bidegrees on $\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$, $\mathbb{P}^n \times \mathbb{P}^m$ in low dimensions, or specific Segre–Veronese settings) are known. Web search did not surface a complete classification.

status_evidence.title: Line bundle - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Line bundles on projective space are classified by integers; products and more general varieties are not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: No complete classification of special line bundles on products of projective spaces is referenced in standard sources.
